clue.text: Familiar form of address for female of the topless sort

definitions.text: Familiar form of address for female

indicators.note: topless means the word for sort loses its top, which in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: a sort or kind is a class

explanation.surface: A cheeky phrase for addressing a woman who goes about without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter C from CLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England and Scotland a girl or young woman is casually called this, as in 'all right, love'.

clue.text: Adolescents throw up after eating out

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other into its middle, as a mouth takes food
up in a down entry means the word for throw is written bottom to top

parts.note: to shy something is to throw it, as at a coconut shy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Teenagers being sick after a meal at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people in their teens are adolescents, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Those having reservations when raising issue about source of coffee?

indicators.note: raising in a down entry lifts the letters so they read from the bottom up
about means the word for issue goes around the coffee source

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
Java is an Indonesian island famed for coffee, which Americans call java

explanation.surface: Someone with doubts when bringing up a question about where their coffee came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservations' looks like doubts but means Native American reservations; 'source of coffee' is a place, not a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Native American people live largely on a large reservation in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Attention-grabbing comment by one article, covered by laying flyer around book

indicators.note: covered by means the following pieces sit inside the bird's name
around means the bird's name is turned round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs
hem is a little cough made to get someone's notice
one is the Roman numeral I
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cough to get attention, beside an object wrapped in feathers by a nesting bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes the bird's name read NEH; 'covered by' places the rest between its E and H.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament book named after the governor who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem.

clue.text: Level 42's doubly so after split

definitions.meaning: flat and smooth, or equal in score
42 is divisible by two, and splitting it gives 4 and 2, both divisible by two as well

explanation.surface: A nod to the band Level 42, said to be doubly so once it split up.
explanation.walkthrough: Level 42 was a British pop band; the clue reads it as the word level beside the number 42.
explanation.definitionFit: A level surface is flat, and an integer divisible by two is called by the same word.

clue.text: Famous Italian actors getting their end away with a star

indicators.note: getting their end away means the word for actors loses its last letter, with a cheeky second meaning

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: Actors having sex with a celebrity: the stuff of tabloid gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting their end away' is British slang for having sex, here cutting the T from CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was an eighteenth-century Venetian adventurer famous for his seductions.

clue.text: Causes embarrassment to party stuck in main elevator

indicators.note: stuck in means the party word is lodged inside the other piece
elevator in a down entry says the word for main is lifted, reading from the bottom up

parts.note: the main is the open sea
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A partygoer trapped in the main lift, red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevator' looks like a lift; in a down entry it lifts the sea word to read AES, and 'stuck in' lodges the party after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them feel ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: King Henry's hobby?

parts.note: Elvis Presley is called the King of rock and roll
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Asking what a monarch named Henry does in his spare time.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Hob; a hob is a sprite or elf, so 'hobby' is read playfully as hob-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A hob is a goblin or sprite of folklore, so something like a hob is fairylike and impish.

clue.text: Show off after second drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Flaunting yourself once you are on your second glass.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport something is to wear or display it proudly, as in sporting a new hat.

clue.text: Food that's regularly vegan? Tosh!

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismissing the idea that some food is routinely vegan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of VEGAN TOSH. With SHOOTS and LEAVES it gives the Lynne Truss book title on punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual word for food or a meal, as in 'grab some ___'.

clue.text: Equity perhaps poorly rated before marriage

indicators.note: poorly suggests the word rated is put together badly, so rearranged

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people

explanation.surface: Fairness, maybe, is not well regarded before a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equity' looks like fairness; it is the British actors' union. 'poorly' rearranges RATED to TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the British trade organisation for actors and performers, an example of a workers' body.

clue.text: Go away with model before she starts photo sessions?

parts.note: shoo is said to chase someone away
the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letter of the word she is used

explanation.surface: A model is told to clear off before she begins her photo shoots.
explanation.walkthrough: With EATS and LEAVES this gives the Lynne Truss book title on punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers book shoots, sessions where pictures are taken of a model or product.

clue.text: Gas with grim smell

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, a gas
dour means stern or grim

explanation.surface: A gas with a nasty smell, as in a stink bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or whiff, especially an unpleasant one, is a plain synonym for smell.

clue.text: Those adding a vital element to 6 and 9

indicators.note: 9 points to the answer at 9 down, which as a verb means to mutate, so these letters change form

parts.note: the number 6 written as a word

explanation.surface: A puzzle reference to agents that add something vital to entries 6 and 9.
explanation.walkthrough: Here '6' is just the number six, not the entry, and '9' is the answer at 9 down, used as the anagram signal on TO SIX AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxidising agents supply oxygen, the element vital for life and combustion, to other substances.

clue.text: More confused, having lost out

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for lost is taken away

parts.note: addled means muddled or confused
L is the abbreviation for lost in sports tables

explanation.surface: Someone getting more befuddled after losing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like a comparative to go with 'confused'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Added means extra or additional, as in added value, so it can stand for more.

clue.text: Wild stab by skinhead, throat getting injured

indicators.note: getting injured suggests the two words are damaged and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent attack by a skinhead leaving someone's throat wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: It is also a Lynne Truss novel, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A random guess made with no information is a stab in the dark, an idiom for guesswork.

clue.text: Flying around currently, or about to be so?

definitions.meaning: airborne at present, like a plane above us
imminent, felt to be on its way, as change can be

explanation.surface: Something airborne right now, or just about to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something aloft, and also something sensed as coming, like rumour or excitement.

clue.text: See 16
Does perhaps find left wing moving right, then left, split by European immigration?

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left

indicators.note: split by means the second copy is broken apart by the European letter going in
the colour of the left is written going right, then again going left, so the second copy runs backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, here coming in

explanation.surface: Wondering if the left drifting rightwards then back is split over European immigration.
explanation.walkthrough: RED is written forwards, then backwards as DER, and 'split by' puts E inside it. 'Does' looks like a verb; it is female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Female deer are called does, so does are examples of this large British deer species.

clue.text: Passed a motion, we hear, to periodically devalue country house

indicators.note: we hear says the word for passing a motion is only heard, spelt another way

parts.note: to pass a motion is to defecate, and shat is its vulgar past tense

indicators.note: periodically picks every other letter of devalue, here the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A meeting voted to lower the value of a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: The French CHAT starts with the sound 'sh'. 'Passed a motion' looks like a vote but is a bodily function.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a castle or large country mansion, often one with vineyards.

clue.text: Weird Scottish medic with desire to follow English League

indicators.note: to follow means the doctor and desire come after the English and League letters

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A strange Scottish doctor itching to join the English League.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for eerie or unearthly, used of ghosts and uncanny sounds.

clue.text: Louvre's first Stubbs? Right, that could describe landscape with more than one mare

definitions.text: that could describe landscape with more than one mare

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Louvre is used

parts.note: Una Stubbs was a British actress, known from Till Death Us Do Part and Sherlock

explanation.surface: Asking whether the Louvre's first Stubbs painting is a landscape full of mares.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stubbs painted horses, so 'mare' looks equine; it is a dark plain on the Moon, plural maria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moon's dark plains are called maria, Latin for seas, so its landscape has many of them.

clue.text: Posh-sounding boy and girl?

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy and a girl with plummy accents.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase mocks an affected, upper-class manner or way of speaking.

clue.text: Goes for some tea, perhaps

definitions.meaning: tea is sold as dried plant foliage, loose in a caddy

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to fetch some tea.
explanation.walkthrough: With EATS and SHOOTS it gives the Lynne Truss book title on punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who departs is said to go off, and loose tea comes as dried foliage from the plant.

clue.text: Foolishly Ian twice bets when not at event

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters are handled without sense, so mixed up
twice means the name Ian is used two times

explanation.surface: Ian keeps placing silly double bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'while away', used when a trial or ceremony goes ahead without the person present.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

definitions.meaning: dishonest or corrupt, as in a crooked copper

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for corrupt, and also a noun for a natural talent or leaning, as in a flair for music.

clue.text: Said what you've got here is an old ball of thread

indicators.note: said means the word for what you are reading is spoken, and spelt differently

parts.note: the solver is reading a crossword clue

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out that what you're holding is an ancient ball of yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: Theseus found his way out of the Minotaur's labyrinth with one, which is why the word gave us 'clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a ball of yarn or string, the origin of the modern sense of a hint.

clue.text: Musical about discontented Tories

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about

indicators.note: discontented means the word Tories has its contents, the inner letters, removed

explanation.surface: A stage show about disgruntled Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: With LUNAR it gives the Lynne Truss book Lunar Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running stage show based on T. S. Eliot's poems about felines.

clue.text: Commonwealth country managed by British? That is regressive

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so these two letters are reversed

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Commonwealth nation is run by Britain, which would be a backward step.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultanate on Borneo that is a member of the association of former British territories.

clue.text: Hole in a tree, right up high

indicators.note: high suggests the words are intoxicated and reeling, so their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A hollow found in a tree, high up on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like height but signals the anagram of A TREE R UP.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or gap, as in a camera's light-admitting opening.
